name: Ladder
line: A campaign in four colours: the hero is four tall colour fields, one per IARC group, and then one full screen per group (red, orange, yellow, grey) saying what the label claims and what it does not, each field growing from a framed panel to full bleed as it arrives, with a huge tone-on-tone numeral, gentle scroll-snap and a slim rail; then the lesson drawn to scale and the explorers drawn in the same colours.
notes: Colour means group and nothing else: red, orange and yellow are Group 1, 2A and 2B wherever they appear (fields, rail, the exposures in the cancer network); Group 3 is a warm grey. 'What it does not say' for 2A and 2B is only the next rung of the scale (2A: not a known cause; 2B: not a probable cause), so no new claims are made. Ivory text on the red field is 6.8:1, ink on orange 5.3:1. The networks are drawn from the explorers' data with a small stable layout written in the page; without JavaScript the explorers' own SVG pictures are shown. Scroll-snap is 'proximity' and is switched off with reduced motion, where the fields are simply full-bleed. Epilogue is Latin-only (no Cyrillic).
